Looking at the cuboid (3×2×2 = 12 cubes), the hatched piece occupies the 2×2 block on top (front‑left), and the white piece occupies the right column: top front, top back, bottom back, plus the hidden bottom‑back‑middle cube (the only way it stays connected).

That leaves the dark piece: the three visible bottom‑front cubes in a row, plus the only remaining hidden cube (bottom‑back‑left), attached to the end of the row.

So the dark shape is a flat "L" tetromino: three cubes in a line with one cube attached at the end, perpendicular to the line.

- A is a flat S/Z shape – no.
- B is a flat L shape (3 in a line + 1 at the end) – yes, matches after rotation.
- C, D, E are either T-shapes or non-planar twists – no.

\boxed{B}
